sections.h2: What does a seller in Lincoln Park have to do that sellers in most Michigan cities do not?
sections.html:
A Lincoln Park seller needs a Certificate of Approval from the city's Building Department before the house can be transferred. The city's ordinance on inspection of residential dwellings prior to sale makes it unlawful to transfer a dwelling, or to act as a broker for the transfer, without a current certificate.

That one rule drives the whole timeline of a sale here, whether you list with an agent, sell on your own or accept a cash offer. The rest of this page explains how the certificate works, then covers the city, its housing figures and the tax and recording steps that follow.

sections.h2: How does the Lincoln Park Certificate of Approval work?
sections.html:
The ordinance (Chapter 1488 of the city's codified ordinances) requires anyone about to transfer a dwelling to register with the Building Department so an inspection can be scheduled. The fee is set by City Council resolution, so ask the department for the current amount.

The main points of the chapter:

  • A Certificate of Approval is valid for one sale or transfer, and a new inspection is required each time the dwelling is sold again.
  • A dwelling includes the house and accessory uses such as garages, sheds, pools, gazebos and playhouses.
  • A buyer may take responsibility for correcting violations by signing a notarized affidavit filed with the Building Department. If the violations are not corrected within six months, occupancy may be prohibited.
  • Failing to obtain the certificate is a municipal civil infraction with a $500 fine.

A transfer means a sale, a land contract or the exercise of an option to purchase. Gifts, devises and lien foreclosures are outside the definition. Rentals follow a separate track, covered below.

sections.h2: How are the certificates for owner-occupied and rental houses different?
sections.html:
Lincoln Park uses different certificates for different situations, and sellers sometimes confuse them. The table summarizes the three named in the ordinance.

Certificates in Lincoln Park Chapter 1488, City of Lincoln Park codified ordinances
CertificateApplies toHow long it lasts
Certificate of ApprovalResidential dwelling being sold or transferredOne sale or transfer
Certificate of ComplianceRental dwellings and rental unitsThree years, unless the property is sold first
Certificate of OccupancyApproved use or occupancy under the zoning ordinancesIssued by the Building Department

A rental that holds a current Certificate of Compliance is not treated as a dwelling for the Certificate of Approval rule, but a new inspection and a new Certificate of Compliance are required before a rental is sold or transferred. If you own a rental, schedule that inspection before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What is Lincoln Park like, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Lincoln Park is a Downriver suburb of Detroit in Wayne County, about 11 miles southwest of downtown. It covers only 5.84 square miles of land, and the 2020 count of 6,896 people per square mile made it the second most densely populated municipality in Michigan, after Hamtramck. The Census Bureau estimates 38,529 residents for July 1, 2025, a 4.3 percent decline from the 2020 base.

Its neighbors are Detroit, Allen Park, Melvindale, Ecorse, Wyandotte and Southgate. The north and south branches of the Ecorse River run through town and join before leaving it. Council Point Park marks the 1763 meeting where Pontiac urged tribal leaders to join him against Fort Detroit.

The city was laid out in 1906 as part of Ecorse Township, became a village in 1921 and a city in 1925. It grew as a bedroom community for workers at the River Rouge Plant and other auto and steel works, and two shopping centers opened in 1955 and 1956. Lincoln Park Public Schools serves residents through Lincoln Park High School, Lincoln Park Middle School and seven elementary schools.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Lincoln Park homes?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 figures describe a compact, owner-heavy city with a modest median value.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $131,000
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 68.8%, with 14,767 households
  • Median gross rent: $1,023
  • Median monthly owner costs: $1,169 with a mortgage, $530 without
  • Same house one year ago: 91.3%
  • Mean commute to work: 24.4 minutes

Those figures, together with a bachelor's degree rate of 11.5 percent and a poverty rate of 21.5 percent, show a price level where a five-figure repair matters a great deal to a net result. Price the house with the inspection list in hand, since a buyer will do the same.

sections.h2: When are Lincoln Park property taxes due?
sections.html:
The city treasurer collects only current-year taxes. Summer bills are mailed by the end of June and fall due August 20, with later installment dates for owners who pay in parts, and a 1 percent penalty applies on the 20th of each month to unpaid summer taxes. Winter bills are mailed around the end of November and are due in mid-February, with a 1 percent monthly penalty after that.

All unpaid taxes transfer to the Wayne County Treasurer on March 1. Online payments carry a 2.95 percent convenience fee charged by the processor, and the city charges $10 for a duplicate tax bill unless you print it from the website. Title companies, agents and landlords are told this in a notice on the city's tax page.

Business personal property is taxed through the same office. Anyone operating on December 31 owes the following year's entire billing cycle, under state law.

sections.h2: How are a Lincoln Park deed and transfer tax handled?
sections.html:
The Wayne County Register of Deeds records Lincoln Park deeds. Deeds and land contracts must generally be tax-certified by the Wayne County Treasurer before they can be recorded, and the office works by appointment. The recording fee for a deed under the schedule that took effect January 1, 2026 is $26 plus a $4 state survey fee where applicable.

State transfer tax is $3.75 per $500 of value, and the county tax is set separately by statute. A transfer from a parent to a child or grandchild, a transfer given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure, and a land contract where title has not passed are among the exemptions listed in state law, so confirm with the title company before you pay.

The buyer files the property transfer affidavit with the assessor within 45 days. As seller, rescind your principal residence exemption within 90 days of moving out. Taxable value resets for the buyer in the year after the transfer.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell my house in Lincoln Park?
faqs.a: Yes. Lincoln Park requires a Certificate of Approval from the Building Department before a dwelling is transferred, and a new one for every sale.

faqs.q: What is the fine for selling without a Certificate of Approval?
faqs.a: The ordinance sets the fine for failing to obtain a Certificate of Approval at $500, as a municipal civil infraction. Other legal remedies still apply.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take over the violations in Lincoln Park?
faqs.a: Yes, by signing a notarized affidavit to correct them. If the violations are not corrected within six months, occupancy may be prohibited.

faqs.q: What does the Census say a Lincoln Park house is worth?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 median value for owner-occupied homes in Lincoln Park is $131,000, with a median gross rent of $1,023.

faqs.q: When do unpaid Lincoln Park taxes go to the county?
faqs.a: All unpaid taxes transfer to the Wayne County Treasurer on March 1. After that, call the county treasurer rather than the city.
